description: Intereses sobre transformación de datos para ayudar a comparar alternativas para una mejora en procesos y decisiones
summary:
AppGro is a web app that uses NASA POWER data from 18 towns in Querétaro, Mexico. Users choose a specific place and a time lapse to analyze rain and temperature record. They can compare information from towns and see when the weather is different as usual. This app also shows when it suffers lack of data. This will help farmers, advisers, and students learn about the climate statistics in the area.
All along the project we use different software for create the app to mention some of them:
•	Python for building the app and FastAPI for the server
•	HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were used for web pages
•	CSV and JSON files helped us to store the data.
Our creative idea was to put NASA data, charts, and tools to compare regional climate records in one app. The data describes a large area, so it may be different from the weather on one farm. The app shows future estimations and experimental ones. It’ll help farmers to understand the climate behavior before making decisions about their crops.
details:
AppGro is a working web app that helps people explore climate information for 18 towns in Querétaro. Users can see past rain and temperature, compare towns, and view climate changes and missing data. The app also shows experimental estimates and lets users explore crop rotation options.

We built AppGro with Python and FastAPI for the server, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web pages. We use NASA POWER data, a statistical model, and CSV and JSON files.

AppGro can give farmers and advisers useful climate information for planning. We checked the model with past data kept for testing. The next step is to work with farmers and specialists and study the app in real farm conditions.

We propose a first group of 18 pilot plots, one in each town. We would record rain and temperature there and compare them with NASA POWER data and our model for the same dates and units. We would also need to record rain, irrigation, and crop results to study water use during crop rotations.

Our team considered missing data, local weather differences, and the limits of climate estimates for farms. These pilot plots would be a first step. More sites may be needed to represent all areas of Querétaro.
